title: P2: merge compares patch-ids, not context-sensitive diff hashes, before and after rebase
spec: Goal T-1383. orchestrator/merge.py _diff_hash (merge.py:11) hashes `git diff --stat` + `git diff --binary` of target...HEAD, which includes hunk line numbers and context, so a clean rebase over an unrelated neighbouring change in the same file flips it and merge() returns rebase_changed_diff (merge.py:52) with no re-review path. Seen twice in luna-inbox on 2026-09-24 (T-0047, T-0057) where `git patch-id --stable` of the reviewed and rebased commits was identical. Change _diff_hash to return the `git patch-id --stable` of `git diff --binary target...HEAD` (pipe the diff into `git patch-id --stable`; empty diff -> a fixed sentinel string, not None; failure of either git call -> None as today). Keep the rebase_changed_diff branch and every other merge behaviour unchanged. Tests in tests/test_merge.py (unittest.TestCase methods): the existing reviewed-rebase test keeps passing (identical upstream content empties the patch -> rebase_changed_diff; unrelated upstream file -> merged); new case: upstream edits a different part of the same file (shifts context/line numbers), the task's patch applies cleanly -> merged, not rebase_changed_diff; new case: upstream change makes the task patch content differ -> rebase_changed_diff.
